page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the right margin: the years 1412, 1443 and 1499, a long note on the causes of degeneration beside "Porrò", and the note "I." with "Providentia Dei" beside "Primùm nempe". Faint marks in the left margin are not printed text.

main_text.p: Aliæ cap.12. JOANNES GALEACIUS, qui Mediolanensis ducatus titulum primus adeptus est, suis carus, hostibus formidolosus, magnam Italiæ partem possedit: quam ingenti virtute & gloria comparaverat. Inter filios, quos reliquit, JOANNES MARIA in ducatu ipsi succedens, Phalaride ipso crudelior, à suis est occisus: GABRIEL spurius, haud amentiâ dispar, amissis Pisis1412,, quas possidebat, Genuæ fecuri palam est percussus: teste Fulgoso lib.3. cap.5.1443. Sic & FRANCISCUS SFORCIA Mediolanensis Dux, omni virtutis genere inter Christianos Principes excelluit. At inter filios natu major GALEACIUS ambitiosus, mulierosus, indignus tanto patre: in PHILIPPO, qui secundus fuit, si corpulentiæ, quam in juventa præ se tulit, par ingenium fuisset; de ejus væcordiâ concitati rumores dicendi minorem materiam præbuissent: LUDOVICUS denique religionis simulator egregius, superbus, avarus, libidinosus, partum armis à patre imperium, à Ludovico XII. Gallorum Rege, cùm numero militum superior esset, victus, XVI die amisit: eodem teste Fulgoso & Egnatio lib.3.cap.5.1499.

Porrò [illegible, ~9 letters] hujus causæ, qui nimirum fiat, quòd parentes optimi pessimos, sapientissimi stultissimos, felicissimi miserrimos suscipiant & relinquant liberos, referri possunt partim ad DEI Opt.Max. providentiam & justitiam: quarum illa ad ea omnia pertinet, quæ ambitu & circuitu mundi continentur; hæc ab hominibus recte facta præmiis ornat, secùs acta pœnis gravissimis vindicat: partim ad Diaboli insidias: partim denique ad hominum negligentem educationem, pravorum consortium, & insolentiam in rebus secundis.Causa, cur liberi à parentum virtute & felicitate degenerent

Primùm nempe DEUS, qui in hoc amplissimo mundi theatro, præter seipsum, nihil esse vult perpetuum, firmum, stabile, immutabile, ejusmodi semper dare solet ludos: ut, quæ vix edita sunt, subitò intereant; quæ jam surrexere, corruant; quæ paululùm floruere, marcescant & tabescant. Hinc videmus, totum hunc mun-I.Providentia Dei

page.notes: The first word of the page, "Aliæ", is partly damaged and marked [?] in the text. The Greek word after "Porrò" is not legible on the scan and is given as an illegible placeholder; it is not transcribed. The running head "Flos IIX." is printed in spaced capitals with the Roman numeral as shown. "fecuri" is a reading of a damaged word and is uncertain. The margin notes 1412, 1443 and 1499 are placed at the lines where they stand. The paragraph ends at the page foot with the printed hyphen of "mun-" and continues on the next page. Show-through and faint stains are not transcribed.
